training.name: Protein Overnight Oats & Berries
training.instructions: Night before: Whisk 50g whey protein into 250g cold almond milk until smooth, then stir in 80g dry rolled oats and refrigerate overnight. Morning: Top with 120g fresh blueberries and a 20g swirl of peanut butter. CEREAL SWAP: Swap rolled oats for Whole-Grain Oat Cereal in the dropdown—just shake the whey + almond milk into 'protein milk' and pour directly over dry cereal and berries.
training.focus: Zero morning cooking; double oats (80g vs 40g on Rest) fuel your 11:00 AM training session.
training.idea: Chilled protein overnight oats or an instant bowl of whole-grain cereal with protein milk and berries.

training.name: Savory Chicken, Basmati Rice & Broccoli Bowl
training.instructions: Reheat a prepped chicken tub with a Training Day basmati rice portion (~330g cooked) and steamed broccoli florets. Drizzle 12g extra virgin olive oil over the hot bowl with garlic powder, dried summer savory, salt, and black pepper.
training.focus: Post-workout glycogen reload—chicken, broccoli, and olive oil stay identical daily while dry rice scales up from 35g to 110g.
training.idea: Batch-prepped savory chicken breast over brown basmati rice and steamed broccoli.

training.name: Cinnamon Crunch Bagel & Whey Shake
training.instructions: Shake 50g whey isolate with 250g cold almond milk. Toast 1 whole sourdough bagel (90g), spread 20g natural peanut butter across both halves, and dust with cinnamon.
training.focus: Fast 2-minute afternoon bridge—eat a full 90g bagel on Training days vs. half a bagel (45g) on Rest days.
training.idea: Chilled almond-milk whey shake paired with a toasted peanut-butter cinnamon bagel.

training.name: Seared Sirloin, Sweet Potato & Roasted Asparagus
training.instructions: Toss 330g cubed sweet potatoes and 150g asparagus with olive oil, salt, and pepper; roast on a sheet pan at 400°F (200°C) for 20–22 minutes (or air-fry). Sear the 230g top sirloin steak in a hot cast-iron skillet for 3–4 minutes per side.
training.focus: Evening recovery dinner—steak, asparagus, and oil stay locked daily while sweet potato scales to 330g (vs 200g on Rest).
training.idea: Seared steak (or salmon/ground beef swap) with roasted sweet potatoes and crisp sheet-pan vegetables.

rest.name: Protein Overnight Oats & Berries
rest.instructions: Night before: Whisk 50g whey protein into 250g cold almond milk until smooth, then stir in 40g dry rolled oats and refrigerate overnight. Morning: Top with 120g fresh blueberries and 20g peanut butter. CEREAL SWAP: Swap rolled oats for Whole-Grain Oat Cereal in the dropdown—shake the whey + almond milk into 'protein milk' and pour directly over 40g dry cereal and berries.
rest.focus: Same zero-cook breakfast as Training days—only the dry oats dial down from 80g to 40g.
rest.idea: Chilled protein overnight oats or an instant bowl of whole-grain cereal with protein milk and berries.

rest.name: Savory Chicken, Basmati Rice & Broccoli Bowl
rest.instructions: Reheat a prepped chicken tub with a Rest Day basmati rice portion (~105g cooked) and steamed broccoli florets. Drizzle 12g extra virgin olive oil over the hot bowl with garlic powder, dried summer savory, salt, and black pepper.
rest.focus: Identical chicken, broccoli, and olive oil as Training days—just grab a smaller Rest Day rice tub (35g dry / ~105g cooked).
rest.idea: Batch-prepped savory chicken breast over a lighter portion of brown basmati rice and steamed broccoli.

rest.name: Cinnamon Crunch Bagel & Whey Shake
rest.instructions: Shake 50g whey isolate with 250g cold almond milk. Toast ½ sourdough bagel (45g—save the other half in a zip bag or freezer for your next Rest day), top with the full 20g peanut butter, and dust with cinnamon.
rest.focus: Exact same shake and peanut butter—just toast ½ bagel (45g) instead of a whole bagel (90g).
rest.idea: Chilled almond-milk whey shake paired with a thick-spread peanut-butter half bagel.

rest.name: Seared Sirloin, Sweet Potato & Roasted Asparagus
rest.instructions: Toss 200g cubed sweet potatoes and 150g asparagus with olive oil, salt, and pepper; roast on a sheet pan at 400°F (200°C) for 20–22 minutes (or air-fry). Sear the 230g top sirloin steak in a hot cast-iron skillet for 3–4 minutes per side.
rest.focus: Same steak, asparagus, and olive oil as Training nights—only the sweet potato dials down from 330g to 200g.
rest.idea: Seared steak (or salmon/ground beef swap) with 200g roasted sweet potatoes and crisp sheet-pan vegetables.

mealPrep.step: 1. Batch-Mix Overnight Oat Jars (5 mins — No Cooking)
mealPrep.details: Line up 3–4 mason jars or sealable containers at a time. Whisk 50g whey protein and 250g unsweetened almond milk in each jar, then stir in 80g rolled oats for Training mornings or 40g rolled oats for Rest mornings. (Whenever you want zero prep, swap oats for cereal in the morning and pour the shaken whey + almond milk straight over the bowl.)

mealPrep.step: 2. Start the Weekly Basmati Rice Batch (~45 mins hands-off)
mealPrep.details: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Rinse 545g of dry whole-grain brown basmati rice (4 × 110g Training + 3 × 35g Rest) under cold water until clear, then start it in your rice cooker.

Trim 1.65 kg of boneless, skinless chicken breasts (7 × 235g raw), coat lightly with spray, and season generously with garlic powder, dried summer savory, paprika, salt, and black pepper. Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 18–22 minutes until 165°F (74°C), rest 10 minutes, and divide evenly into 7 identical lunch containers—no separate Training vs. Rest chicken weights needed.

mealPrep.step: 4. Portion & Freeze Rice Tubs (The Only Labeled Tubs)
mealPrep.details: Fluff the cooked basmati rice, let steam escape for 5 minutes, and weigh into freezer-safe tubs: 4 Training tubs (~330g cooked each) and 3 Rest tubs (~105g cooked each). Reheat from frozen in 90–120 seconds with a 1-teaspoon splash of water.

Cube your weekly sweet potatoes (1,920g total peeled/cubed: 4 × 330g for Training nights + 3 × 200g for Rest nights) and snap the woody ends off your asparagus. Store in sealed fridge containers so weeknight dinner goes onto a sheet pan in 2 minutes.

mealPrep.step: 6. Set Up the Countertop Bagel & Shake Station
mealPrep.details: Keep sourdough bagels, natural peanut butter, cinnamon, and whey isolate clustered together. Pre-slice 2 bagels in half for Rest days (45g per half) so grabbing either a whole bagel (90g) or half bagel (45g) at 3:30 PM requires zero thought.

guidelines: Front-load early: Drink 500-750 g (ml) within the first hour of waking.
Anchor to meals: Have 400-500 g (ml) (~1 bottle) with each main meal.
Check the gauge: Aim for urine that is pale straw to light yellow.
